paper.title: A priori bounds and degeneration of Herman rings with bounded type rotation number
paper.page_convention: PDF and printed page numbers agree; 59 pages

summary: One Major core proof defect and two Minor construction or applicability defects are established. Verified repairs preserve the relevant gain, finite-prefix existence, and scale dependence. No principal-theorem counterexample was established; the prescribed-time bridge and width inequality retain their precise proof limits.

problems.title: Overly narrow almost-tiling gap selection

source_location.section: Theorem 5.1 deep-case proof; same selection in Lemma 6.2

problems.original_claim: For tau=10, choose N=floor(lambda/(3 tau^2)) almost-tiling pieces with consecutive gaps in ((tau-1)l_n,tau l_n].
assumptions: bounded-type rotation; golden mean is allowed with B=1
even n>=8, arbitrarily deeper than the finite deep-case threshold
level-n pieces of positive angular length l_n, time indices 0<=i<q_(n+1)
fixed sufficiently large lambda with N>=5

decisive_check.type: general analytic arithmetic obstruction plus retained exact finite checks
decisive_check.argument: Consecutive-convergent unimodularity restricts allowed index steps to A=4q_n-4q_(n-1) and B=2q_n-5q_(n-1). The two starting bands and the dead band reached after A,B imply at most three steps/four pieces. A circular large forward gap is excluded because one gap >=1-11l_n plus three gaps >10l_n would total >1. Bounds r in [3/5,5/8] hold at every even n>=8.
decisive_check.computation_execution: Recovered historical original-reviewer exact computations; no rerun falsely claimed in this continuation

counterevidence: The witness refutes the intermediate combinatorial selection, not the conditional large-width theorem.
No rational map with arbitrarily large width satisfying all theorem hypotheses was constructed.
The widened window has the same strict lower separation and same N.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem6.1 -> Proposition4.2 -> Theorem5.1 deep-case Quasi-Additivity gain -> Theorem8.1 doubling -> Corollary8.2 and TheoremA, pp44-46.
problems.impact_boundary: Original invalid combinatorial input is in the core amplification proof, hence Major. The wider-window replacement retains the exact sqrt(N/2)K gain and parameter dependence; no principal theorem counterexample is claimed.

repair.verification: L<(tau+2)Nl_n and (tau+1)(tau+2)N<=132lambda/300<lambda retain all required containments and the same N; offset remains O_B(log lambda). Lemma6.2 fixed constants may be enlarged.

problems.title: Degenerate finite-prefix first-return construction
problems.original_claim: The every-n first-return proof uses an enlarged interval with endpoints c_(q_n-q_(n-1)) and c_(q_(n-1)).
assumptions: unicritical boundary realization f_theta selected by Theorem C/Corollary9.5
unique free critical point c0=1 with local degree d; cj=f^j(c0) on irrational Herman curve

decisive_check.argument: At n=2 both endpoints equal c1, so the stated nondegenerate shortest interval and its pointed collar do not exist. At n=1 the target equals an endpoint. Reading N as starting at 0 or 1 does not remove n=2.
decisive_check.computation_execution: Historical exact calculations retained; current source images and bounded analytic repair checked.

counterevidence: This refutes the printed initial construction, not existence of suitable return domains.
The n>=4 construction and asymptotic Corollary10.3 are unaffected by a finite prefix.
problems.core_dependency: Pointed first-return domains used in Section10; Sections3-9 and the asymptotic limit do not depend on these three initial choices.
problems.impact_boundary: Finite-prefix domain construction only; explicit uniform repair preserves every-n statement for the intended maps.

repair.statement: For n<=3 choose uniformly separated concentric target disks in the normalized quasiconformal coordinate, then take the connected pullback containing c0.
repair.verification: q_n<=(B+1)^3 and bounded-type separation isolate the sole critical value. Connected monodromy gives degree d, Riemann-Hurwitz gives disks, and the collar/Koebe/quasisymmetry estimates preserve bounded shape and scale.

problems.title: Siegel-scale cutoff starts one level too early
problems.original_claim: After l_(M+1)<=mu<l_M, all n>=M are called Siegel scale.

decisive_check.argument: At n=M, l_M>mu contradicts the required l_n<=mu.

counterevidence: Setting S=M+1 restores the exact scale condition.
The transition losses C1=C(tau-1), C2(t)=4C^(tm+1) and uniform modulus dependence remain valid.
problems.core_dependency: Applicability of the scale transition in Lemmas8.3-8.4, which contributes to TheoremA.
problems.impact_boundary: One-level correction retains the quantitative argument; no TheoremA counterexample.

repair.statement: Use N<=n<S for Herman scale and n>=S for Siegel scale, S=M+1; replace the undefined N1 cutoff by S.

clarifications.checked_result: The finite-cover middle-cut extension gives Z^(a+b)<=Z^a+C under proper disk cover, full/disjoint marked continua, controlled topology, and local degree>=2. Choose m>=k0 before the stopping argument; then choose Q sufficiently late, and absorb C with eta=delta/8.

clarifications.checked_result: The necessary horizontal-plus-vertical width inequality has a direct essential-arc restriction proof under full/disjoint/compact-containment assumptions.

independent_acceptance_review.scope: Independent focused acceptance of all three reported problems, the stated proof supplements and remaining dependency limits in Willie Rush Lim's arXiv:2302.07794v5,9 September2025,59pages. Root actually read and inspected every page of the current seven-page report. The native helper independently checked the exact combinatorial assumptions, finite-prefix counterexamples, source dependencies and cited local repairs. No equivalence to an unavailable publisher version or complete verification of all external theorems is asserted.

problems.independent_check: For golden-mean rotation, tau=10 and every sufficiently deep even n, the literal consecutive-gap window(9 l_n,10 l_n] permits at most four almost-tiling pieces. Writing q=q_n,p=q_(n-1), unimodularity restricts forward initial-point steps to A=4q-4p and B=2q-5p. The allowed starting bands and their images exclude a fourth step. The proof covers circular shortest-distance readings and endpoint conventions. For any fixed large lambda with N=floor(lambda/(3 tau^2))>=5, an allowed even n lies beyond the finite deep-case thresholds, so the required N pieces cannot be selected.
problems.assumptions: The exact continued-fraction convention, positive piece length l_n, time-index range0<=i<q_(n+1) and arbitrary bounded-type golden-mean rotation are retained. The proof is analytic for all sufficiently deep even n; finite exact checks only corroborate it.
problems.counterevidence: This refutes the intermediate combinatorial construction, not a rational map satisfying an arbitrary large-width hypothesis and not Theorem A itself.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem6.1 and Proposition4.2 feed the deep-case Quasi-Additivity argument in Theorem5.1; its gain enters Theorem8.1, Corollary8.2 and TheoremA(pp44-46). The invalid selection is therefore in an actual core proof.
problems.repair: A greedy selection enlarges the upper gap to11 l_n. The same N is retained because(tau+1)(tau+2)N<=132 lambda/300<lambda; the same square-root-in-N gain and parameter dependence survive. The analogous fixed constants in Lemma6.2 can also be enlarged.
problems.severity_rationale: A verified local repair is recorded separately and does not erase the demonstrated invalid derivation in the core proof. The previous Minor assessment is superseded.

problems.independent_check: Theorem10.2's initial enlarged interval has endpoints c_(q_n-q_(n-1)) and c_(q_(n-1)). For golden-mean q0=q1=1,q2=2, both endpoints equal c1 atn2; atn1 the requested target is an endpoint. The finite-prefix ambiguity disappears atn>=4, when the enlarged arc has length2 l_(n-1)+l_n<1/2.
problems.assumptions: The return-map argument is for the unicritical boundary realization supplied by TheoremC, with its single free critical point and the stated bounded-type quasiconformal control; it is not extended to an arbitrary multicritical map.
problems.counterevidence: This is a finite-prefix construction defect, not proof that the asserted return map cannot exist. Corollary10.3 uses a subsequential limit and is unchanged after deleting finitely many levels.
problems.repair: Uniform finite-prefix orbit separation, normalized quasiconformal conjugacy, two nested disks, single critical-value monodromy and Riemann-Hurwitz yield the proper disk cover of degreed; Koebe distortion supplies the pointed-shape bounds. The rescaling uses rotated z^d in Riemann coordinates, not a generic no-degree-loss assertion from shape alone.
problems.severity_rationale: The exact defect is restricted to the finite prefix; the actual asymptotic core use survives with the verified bounded replacement.

problems.independent_check: Equation(8.1) defines l_(M+1)<=mu<l_M but the text calls every n>=M Siegel scale, although n=M has l_M>mu. With S=M+1, the valid split is n<S and n>=S; the undefined N1 in Lemma8.3 is replaced byS.
problems.counterevidence: This is an applicability mismatch, not a numerical counterexample to the a priori bound. The neighboring-level estimate on sourcep46 absorbs the same fixed transition factor.
problems.repair: The passage through S<=n1<S+tm and mu/l_(n1+1)<=C^(tm+1) preserves the order of choices and fixed transition losses.
problems.severity_rationale: The one-level cutoff correction preserves the actual quantitative transition argument; no separate core loss is asserted.

local_checks.check: The prescribed-time bridge from Proposition7.2's stopping time to q_(n+m2) is supported under the actual proper-disk-cover, disjoint full marked-continuum and local-degree hypotheses. The chosen time offset ensures enough precritical encounters; parameter choices remain noncircular. No unrestricted branched-map width monotonicity is assumed.

The required horizontal-plus-vertical width inequality is supported by the explicit first-transition/overflow/canonical-restriction argument. This does not establish the stronger literal domain inclusion(6.3), for which neither proof nor counterexample was obtained.

The hull/covering discussion supplies no valid counterexample to the relevant Covering statement. Peripheral E-absorption and quantitative outer-buffer reidentification remain only partly reconstructed; these audit limits are not promoted to confirmed defects.

The parallel-sum grading identity, scalar contraction, noncircular amplification order, bounded-type dependence and unicritical algebra are consistent within the preserved bounded checks. No existence for every algebraic parameter or proof of ConjectureD is claimed.
